problem: Existing ALFRED agents are either end-to-end neural policies (data-hungry, memory-less over long horizons) or map-based planners with binary cell maps that need hand-crafted rules to fix perception errors and to handle things like openable receptacles.
motivation: Household mobile manipulation needs a scene representation that is semantic (objects and affordances), updated online, easy to query and generalizable to unseen scenes. Long trajectories with rare semantic targets in egocentric views also make purely neural control hard to learn from limited data.
key_idea: Learn a soft, gradient-optimized grid scene representation of object and affordance semantics on the fly, and use it for map-based coarse navigation followed by a short-horizon neural fine controller for interaction.
insight: Replacing the differentiable map with binary cell maps drops unseen-valid SR from 55.0 to 42.7, so soft, online-optimized semantics that balance history and current observation matter more than hand-crafted fixes. Removing coarse control collapses SR to 9.1, while removing fine control costs about 3-4 points, so global analytic navigation does the bulk of the work and the neural policy handles local refinement. Ground-truth perception plus language lifts unseen SR to 79.6, and language errors are the largest failure cause (about 19%), so perception and language parsing are the remaining bottlenecks.
method: Perception: Mask R-CNN (85 classes) for instance segmentation and two U-Nets for depth (50 bins of 10 cm) and affordance (1 navigable + 7 interactive classes). All are trained on simulator-oracle labels from training scenes only, from egocentric RGB.

Differentiable scene representation: 80x80 grid (25 cm cells, 20 m x 20 m), each with a 256-d embedding s_i, plus N^o+N^a learnable semantic query vectors q_j. Class probability is sigmoid(s_i^T q_j); s_i is zero-initialized and q_j random, so p starts at 0.5.

On-the-fly optimization: Semantic point clouds are projected top-down to give soft grid labels (normalized class proportion, Eq. 1). Visible grids (>500 points) are updated by gradient descent on both s and q (10 iterations, lr 0.01) at each step.

Random walk + coarse control: If the target has not been detected, the agent walks to random navigable waypoints via BFS on the navigability map. Once it is detected, the grid with the highest object-times-affordance probability is targeted, and BFS navigates to within 1 m of it.

Fine control: A ResNet50 takes RGB, estimated depth and the target mask, and per-object classifiers output navigation actions or Interact. The agent first rotates to face the localized target. It is trained by behavior cloning on 316,935 expert frames within 4 steps of interaction, versus 1,051,308 frames in the default ALFRED trajectories.
Language and planning: FILM's fine-tuned BERTs predict task type and arguments from the goal directive. Templates convert these into verb-noun subgoals. Step-by-step instructions are optional.
Affordance-driven interaction: The openable affordance is detected automatically to decide whether to open a receptacle, replacing hand-crafted tests.

setting.backbone: Mask R-CNN + U-Net (depth, affordance) + ResNet50 fine policy + BERT (from FILM); scene representation optimized online
setting.training_data: ALFRED training-scene frames with AI2THOR oracle labels (depth, 85-class segmentation, affordance); 316,935 expert-planner frames for the fine policy; BERT from FILM; Mask R-CNN initialized from COCO
setting.observation: egocentric RGB 300x300 (depth, segmentation and affordance are estimated); pose from accumulated discrete actions
setting.action_space: discrete ALFRED actions (MoveAhead, Rotate, LookUp/Down, plus composed MoveLeft/Right/Back and interaction actions); BFS on a map for coarse navigation
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT depth, segmentation, affordance and language are used only in ablations); the expert planner is used for training data only

results: DISCO gets 54.7 SR on ALFRED test-unseen with only the goal directive, above the strongest baselines, which use step-by-step instructions (CAPEAM 46.1, Prompter 45.7), and 56.5 with step-by-step instructions. PLWSR of 35.5-36.5 in unseen scenes is roughly 1.75x Prompter's, showing much better efficiency.
limitations: Simulator-only evaluation with a discretized symbolic action space in AI2THOR, so sim2real and real robot kinematics are not addressed.
Relies on template-based task planning and BERT parsing tailored to ALFRED, and language errors cause about 19% of failures. Perception and depth are supervised with simulator oracle labels.
Failures include navigation collisions (14% in unseen), objects inside closed receptacles that are never found, and weak performance on Stack tasks (27.5% SR in unseen).
